newsitem.title: USA: XATA sees Q4, FY97 net losses with charge.
newsitem.headline: XATA sees Q4, FY97 net losses with charge.

text.p: XATA Corp said it expects to report a net loss for its fiscal fourth quarter and fiscal year ending September 30 after taking a charge to revalue certain assets.
The maker of onboard information systems for trucks said it expects fourth-quarter net sales to be less than those reported a year ago of $3.16 million.

"The company's profitability in fiscal 1997 has ... been adversely affected by operating losses and depreciation and amortization expenses related to two acquisitions completed in August and October of 1996," XATA said.

XATA on Tuesday reported net sales for its fiscal third quarter of $2.8 million, versus $2.4 million in the comparable year-ago period. Net income for the fiscal third quarter was $22,241, or $0.01 per share, compared with $332,509, or $0.07 per share, in the fiscal 1996 third quarter.

Growth in the private fleet business enabled XATA to achieve an increase in third quarter net sales despite an expected decline in deliveries to a major customer that had accounted for over 50 percent of net sales in the fiscal 1996 third quarter, the company said.

"This strong growth in our private fleet business has been masked by the slowdown in deliveries to our single largest customer," XATA said. "While this customer continues to purchase and install our products, the implementation program proceeds at a slower pace than we experienced in the prior fiscal year. As a result of this slower pace, we will be forecasting our revenue from this customer more conservatively in coming quarters."
XATA said that during the fiscal fourth quarter it will will take a non-recurring, non-cash charge, primarily to reflect a revaluation of assets acquired from Payne & Associates in August 1996.

"While this charge will result in a net loss for the fourth quarter and fiscal year ending September 30, 1997, it will also eliminate goodwill and software development amortization expenses that have been a drag on our profitability," the company said.
